findings: Current Afwijkingenbeleid Eemsdelta 2025 explicitly defines kamergewijze verhuur and contains substantive assessment rules.
Splitting, including kangoeroewoningen, is possible only when the general residential criteria are met and the result remains one main building without changing the pre-split appearance/build form.
Kamergewijze verhuur is not allowed unless current housing policy provides room for it and all other criteria are satisfied.
A main building is in principle used for one separate household.
This closes the generic question whether Eemsdelta has a municipality-specific current substantive assessment framework.

findings: Current Omgevingsplan gemeente Epe CVDR696234 is confirmed current from 15-01-2026 and warns that related regulations are juridically part of the plan.
Current Beleidsregels kaders woningsplitsing en tijdelijke bewoning van bijgebouwen provide a substantive splitting framework.
Within existing urban area, splitting is limited to the main building of detached ground-bound dwellings; recreational and company dwellings are excluded.
After splitting each dwelling must have at least 55 m2 use area; building mass is not enlarged and the appearance/build form remains one erf; heritage values are preserved where relevant.
For former farms outside the urban context, landscape integration, housing-policy fit, minimum 55 m2 and sufficient parking are among the criteria.
The policy explicitly says woningsplitsing is not kamerverhuur and that kamerverhuur has its own regulation in the Omgevingsplan.
A separate current Beleidskader Kavelsplitsing gemeente Epe is effective from 27-01-2026, useful for distinguishing dwelling splitting from parcel splitting.
